en.name: Damian
en.summary: Early physician-martyr who, with his twin brother Cosmas, treated the sick without payment and became one of the most venerated healing saints in Christian history.
en.body: Damian and his twin brother Cosmas were, by tradition, physicians of Arab origin practicing in the Roman province of Syria in the early fourth century, known throughout their region for treating patients entirely free of charge, an approach to medicine so distinctive it earned them the title "unmercenary healers" in Eastern Christian tradition, and their reputation for both medical skill and evident holiness drew converts alongside patients. Their growing following brought them to the attention of Roman authorities during the persecution under Diocletian, and after surviving several reported attempts at execution, they were ultimately beheaded together around 287. Devotion to the brothers spread widely across both Eastern and Western Christianity in the centuries following their deaths, with numerous churches, including a major basilica in Rome, dedicated to them jointly, and their names remain paired in the Roman Canon of the Mass alongside the apostles and other early martyrs. Physicians and surgeons have long invoked the twins together as patrons of the healing profession.
